I've been working this land in Quzhou for 25 years. My 14 mu runs wheat from October through early June, then I turn it straight over to maize until late September. Same ground, two crops every year. That's how everyone here does it, and it's what the land knows.

For **wheat**, I'll plant in early October like always. I get my improved seeds from the county seed station — a semi-dwarf high-yielding variety that does well in our soils. I'll rotary-till after the maize harvest to chop up the stubble before seeding. I spread compound fertilizer as a base when I plant, then topdress with urea at jointing in late March. Three irrigations: one at sowing to get a good stand, one at jointing, one at heading. I spray herbicide in late winter when the weeds come up, then hit it again at heading for aphids and rust — that's two pesticide passes. If I do this right, I expect around 450 jin per mu. Good year, maybe 500.

For **maize**, I plant immediately after wheat harvest in early June. No time to waste — the growing season is short. I use hybrid seed, always.郑单958 or something similar from the local supply co-op. Summer has more rain so I only irrigate twice — once if it's dry at emergence, and again at silking when the plant really needs water. I topdress nitrogen heavily at the big bell stage. Post-emergence herbicide early, then watch for corn borers — two pesticide rounds. I'll rotary-till again before winter wheat goes back in. Maize should give me around 550 kg per mu.

My household is 6 people. This rotation keeps me busy all year but it's steady and I know how to do it.
